todo: Obtain qualified-human citation verification for the proposed aphakia to visual-impairment association.
Confirm the aphakia phenotype, objective visual-acuity or visual-field deficit, chronology, age/developmental context, optical rehabilitation, and alternative ocular explanations before publication.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-27 adds this relationship only as a bounded visual-outcome association. Aphakia, especially congenital or pediatric aphakia, can be associated with reduced visual development or impaired visual outcome, but the diagnosis alone does not establish a particular person's visual impairment or its severity. Require documented aphakia, separately measured compatible visual impairment, relevant laterality and developmental chronology, and review of amblyopia, corneal disease, glaucoma, retinal or optic-nerve disease, refractive error, surgical complications, and optical-rehabilitation history. Do not infer visual impairment from an aphakia label alone.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of aphakia and objectively measured visual impairment
Laterality, age at onset, developmental chronology, visual-acuity/field results, and relevant surgical history
Assessment of amblyopia, glaucoma, corneal disease, retinal or optic-nerve disease, refractive error, and other ocular contributors
Documentation of optical correction or rehabilitation and its effect on measured function

Resolution of publication guard: Require documented aphakia, separately measured compatible visual impairment, relevant laterality/chronology, and competing ocular-cause review; do not infer impairment from aphakia alone.

sourceReferences.citation: Ernst J, et al. Congenital primary aphakia. J AAPOS. 2022;26(1):4.e1-4.e5. PMID 35051625. doi:10.1016/j.jaapos.2021.09.008.
sourceReferences.note: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-27 case-series evidence for the bounded aphakia visual-outcome proposition. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source remains pending qualified-human review.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 35051625; congenital primary aphakia case series describing natural history, management, and visual outcomes; approved ME-27 guard requires objective visual impairment and competing ocular-cause review.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The congenital aphakia case series supports a relationship between aphakia phenotype and visual outcome, but does not establish a deterministic or individual visual-impairment pathway.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established; objective visual testing, developmental chronology, treatment history, and competing ocular diagnoses require individual review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Absence of the crystalline lens can alter optical focus and, in congenital or early-onset cases, visual development; the extent of any resulting functional visual impairment remains phenotype- and treatment-dependent and is hypothesized for an individual until objectively documented.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Aphakia-related visual outcome depends on onset, laterality, developmental factors, ocular comorbidity, and rehabilitation; the source does not prove an individual's visual impairment was caused by aphakia.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Aphakia and objective visual impairment; laterality and developmental chronology; acuity or visual-field measurements; optical rehabilitation; amblyopia, glaucoma, retinal, optic-nerve, corneal, refractive, surgical, and other ocular contributors.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: surgical complications or other ocular disease
